links_touching_record.rationale: The ASIL D requirement specifies how many consecutive violations confirm a fault but says nothing about a partially advanced counter when the value returns in range. That silence is the root cause of the implementation divergence this change corrects.

The SOA design already specifies the DEBOUNCING -> IDLE transition with the action reset_debounce, so the design is correct and is not revised. It is a declared target of the change because the divergence was located here and the absence of a revision is a decision that belongs on the record.

The software requirement an implementation is actually written against is silent on counter reset, and its acceptance criteria are a copy of the safety requirement's. The new fail-able reset criterion must be added in both places.

The limit-monitor test performs its two violations back to back and only then an in-range sample, so it never observes a partially advanced counter at the moment of recovery. The defect is not expressible in the current step structure, which is why the measure is a declared target and not a regression to re-run.

integrity.anchor_registry_note: The corpus provenance gate verifies each anchor against the file that anchor names and stores no registry-level digest of its own. This digest is recorded so a signature also pins which anchor set was in force.
integrity.verbatim_block_note: The block in section 3 is the file's decoded text with any single trailing newline removed, which is what the markdown fences require. `record_sha256` above is over the raw file bytes and is the digest a signature refers to; this one is over the text as embedded, so a verifier can compare either.

outcome_record._ledger_note: packet_first_commit is the git commit that FIRST contained the archived signed packet. It proves WHEN and IN WHAT STATE the packet was committed. It does NOT prove who read it, and nothing in the corpus makes an approval unforgeable. See docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md
outcome_record._note: Fields a human or a later process may fill AFTER a signature exists. Empty here; present so the outcome can be captured without editing the generator. Since APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1 the decision is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl, and these fields cross-reference that entry rather than being the record of it.

affected_artifact_rationale.current_text_binding: Statement: 'monitor each cell voltage against configured minimum and maximum limits with a debounce of 2 consecutive violations within 100 ms'. Acceptance criteria: limit check latency 5 ms, limit accuracy 1 mV, debounce filtering 1E-6 events/hour against sigma=5 mV noise, FAULT request latency 2 ms.
affected_artifact_rationale.not_changed: The 5 ms classification latency, the 1 mV limit accuracy and the 2 ms FAULT request latency are unaffected; a counter clear is a constant-time operation and is not on the critical path. The 2-consecutive count itself is deliberately left alone: CR-001 owns the count, and two changes must not both move it in the same baseline.
affected_artifact_rationale.what_changes: The requirement is amended to state the reset semantics explicitly: the consecutive-violation count shall be cleared when a sample returns within limits, and a confirmed violation shall require consecutive violations without an intervening in-range sample. The 1E-6 events/hour false-positive criterion is re-stated to include the recovery case, because the reported failure mode is a false positive that the current criterion does not mention.
affected_artifact_rationale.why_re_review: This is the ASIL D requirement and it is the level at which the ambiguity actually lives. It specifies how many consecutive violations are needed to confirm, and says nothing about what happens to a partially advanced count when the value returns in range. The requirement is therefore the root cause of the divergence: an implementation that never resets conforms to the requirement as written.

affected_artifact_rationale.current_text_binding: State machine IDLE, CHECKING, DEBOUNCING, VIOLATION_CONFIRMED, FAULT_TRIGGERED. The transition DEBOUNCING -> IDLE is specified as trigger 'back_in_limits', guard 'voltage within limits', action 'reset_debounce'. Constraint: 'Debounce count configurable (default: 2)'.
affected_artifact_rationale.not_changed: Every element: the state set, all six transitions including DEBOUNCING -> IDLE, the guards, the actions, and the 'reset_debounce' action itself. The design is baselined at revision 1 and stays there.
affected_artifact_rationale.what_changes: Nothing. Explicitly nothing, and that is the finding.
affected_artifact_rationale.why_no_revision: This is the substantive difference between this record and its scenario fixture, which raises the design to revision 2. A revision that changes nothing inflates the revision history and destroys the ability to tell, from the revision number alone, whether the design was ever in question. The divergence is recorded against the implementation, which is where it is.
affected_artifact_rationale.why_re_review: Not because the design is wrong - because the design is right and the record must say so. The design already specifies the transition and the action that the implementation omits, so the design is not revised. It is reviewed once more to confirm the specification is unambiguous about the action, and that confirmation is recorded here as a finding of 'no change required' rather than as a new revision.

affected_artifact_rationale.current_text_binding: Statement: 'compare against configured minimum (2.5V) and maximum (4.2V) limits with a debounce of 2 consecutive violations within 100 ms'. Acceptance criteria mirror FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 one for one.
affected_artifact_rationale.not_changed: The acquisition source, the comparison itself and the classification latency are unaffected. The 2-consecutive count is left alone for the same reason as above.
affected_artifact_rationale.what_changes: A new acceptance criterion is added for counter reset on return to in-range, and the criterion is stated in terms a unit test can fail: after any number of sub-threshold excursions each followed by an in-range sample, the next single excursion shall not confirm a violation.
affected_artifact_rationale.why_re_review: The software requirement is the one an implementation is actually written against, and it is silent on reset for the same reason the safety requirement is. Its acceptance criteria are a copy of the safety requirement's, which means the missing criterion is duplicated in both places and must be added in both.

affected_artifact_rationale.current_text_binding: Step 1: 'Inject cell voltage 4300 mV (above 4200 mV limit)' expecting the debounce counter to increment. Step 2: 'Repeat injection 2 times (debounce count)' expecting a FAULT request. Step 3: 'Inject voltage 4100 mV (within limits)' expecting no fault. referenced_requirements: FB2-SAF-FSR-000002, FB2-SW-SWR-000002.
affected_artifact_rationale.not_changed: Test level, method and referenced requirements are unchanged. Steps 1 to 3 are retained: they still verify the positive path, and removing them would lose the confirmation coverage that this measure exists to provide.
affected_artifact_rationale.what_changes: A recovery sequence is added: several sub-threshold excursions, each separated by an in-range sample, followed by a final in-range sample, expecting no FAULT request; and a follow-on single excursion expecting no FAULT request, which is the case that currently fails. The added steps are the ones that fail before the correction and pass after, which is what makes the re-execution evidence.
affected_artifact_rationale.why_re_review: The test's structure is why the defect survived. It performs its two violations back to back and only then an in-range sample, so the counter is never observed in a partially advanced state at the moment of recovery. A missing reset is only observable in a sequence where an excursion is followed by a recovery, repeatedly, and the current test contains no such step.

decision.decision_maker: change_control_board chair, fictional role identity 'A. Renner' (synthetic scenario character; not a foxBMS maintainer, not SoftwareDevLabs staff, not a real person)
decision.rationale: Dispositioned approved as a defect correction with a deliberately narrow work scope. The board fixes three things and refuses one. Fixed: the software requirement is clarified to state the reset semantics explicitly, because a requirement that is silent on reset cannot constrain an implementation; the safety requirement is clarified in the same terms so the two do not diverge again; and the test is extended with the recovery sequence, because a defect that the verification set could not express cannot be shown fixed by a test that still cannot express it. Refused: no new design element. FB2-SW-DSN-000002 already specifies the DEBOUNCING -> IDLE transition with the reset_debounce action, so revising the design would add a revision that changes nothing and would make the record of what the design already required harder to read. The correction is to the implementation and to the requirement that left the behaviour open, and this record is also the precondition for baselining the CR-001 debounce increase.

record_verbatim.evidence_reference_note: impact_analysis.affected_evidence is empty by schema, not by omission. The change schema admits only ids matching ^FB2-EVD-[A-Z]{2,4}-[0-9]{6}$, and no artifact with an FB2-EVD- prefix exists in either profile. The execution this change invalidates is FB2-VER-EXE-000001, which does exist in synthetic_reference; it is named in evidence_invalidation above rather than forced into a slot whose id scheme does not admit it.

impact_analysis.risk_assessment: The safety exposure is availability and trust, not a missing safety function, and the distinction matters for how the fix is reviewed. (1) No hazard is created: the protective reaction still occurs, and it occurs sooner than it should. FB2-SAF-HAZ-000001 lists 'All HV contactors open' and 'Vehicle propulsion disabled' as safe states for the cell-voltage hazard, and a spurious entry into those states is a conservative failure in the safety sense. (2) The exposure is that the ASIL D path becomes untrustworthy. A monitor that reports a fault that is not present trains the operator and the service technician to disregard it, and a de-energised contactor under load at an arbitrary moment is itself a wear event. The realistic field consequence is repeated, unjustified loss of propulsion that a technician cannot reproduce, which is a maintenance-attrition failure mode rather than a hazard. (3) The mechanism is a design-implementation divergence, not a design defect. FB2-SW-DSN-000002 already specifies the transition DEBOUNCING -> IDLE, triggered by 'back_in_limits', guarded by 'voltage within limits', with the action 'reset_debounce'. The design is correct and complete on this point; the implementation does not perform the action the design names. That is why this record does not revise the design, and it is a materially different finding from a missing design element. (4) The requirement permitted the divergence. FB2-SW-SWR-000002 states 'a debounce of 2 consecutive violations within 100 ms' and FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 repeats it, and neither says what happens to a partially advanced counter when the value returns in range. A requirement that specifies the trigger count but not the reset semantics leaves the reset behaviour unspecified, which is how an implementation that never resets can pass a conformance review. (5) Verification did not catch it. FB2-VER-TMS-000001 exercises an excursion, a repetition, and then a single in-range value; it never performs a sequence of excursions each followed by recovery, which is the only sequence in which a missing reset is observable. (6) Interaction with CR-001: raising the debounce count from 2 to 3 as commissioned by FB2-MAN-CHG-000001 makes this defect worse, not better, because the counter is advanced more often and survives more opportunities to be wrongly confirmed. Fixing the reset is a precondition of baselining the new debounce count, not a parallel activity.

record_verbatim.record_purpose: This is the change-management record of record for the synthetic-reference project. It is not a test fixture: the change-lifecycle demonstration of the same subject (docs/artifacts/scenarios/change-lifecycles/change-003-software-defect.json, FB2-SCN-CHG-000003) exists separately to exercise the corpus scenario gate, and the two are intentionally different artifacts with different jobs.

differences_that_matter: The fixture revises the design to revision 2; this record does not, because the design already specifies the reset and is therefore not in question. This is the substantive engineering difference between the two artifacts.
The fixture uses change_type 'software_behavioral_defect', which the change schema's enumeration does not admit; this record uses 'software_behavior' and says why.
The fixture places the code id in the artifact lists; this record keeps it in implementation_target, because an anchor is not an artifact.

This record adds the false-positive consequence analysis, the explicit statement that no change to the hazard is expected, the ordering constraint against CR-001, and the requirement that the added regression step be shown to fail before the fix - which is the condition that turns a re-run into evidence of a fix.

reverification_criterion.acceptance_condition: Re-verification is complete when the added recovery sequence in FB2-VER-TMS-000001 has been executed against the corrected implementation and passes, and the same sequence has been shown to fail against the uncorrected implementation. The second half is the part that is easy to skip and is the only thing that distinguishes evidence of a fix from evidence of a re-run. Both conditions are currently unmet: nothing has been executed.

excluded.basis: the plausibility test operates on the acquisition path upstream of the limit comparison and has no path to the debounce counter

selected.basis: direct - the only measure of the limit monitor, and the one whose step structure must change to express the defect at all

regression - the contactor reaction is where a spurious FAULT becomes a physical event; this measure is the end-to-end detector of the reported behaviour and its result is what an operator would actually experience

reverification_criterion.selection_rule: Select every test measure whose stimulus can express the defect, plus the end-to-end measure that would show the consequence, because a fix to a debounce counter can only be shown by a test that sequences recovery between excursions.

record_verbatim.title: Change Record CR-003: SOA Debounce Counter Not Reset on Return to In-Range Voltage (Design-Implementation Divergence)

trigger.description: A transient voltage excursion above the configured limit advances the debounce counter, and when the voltage returns within limits the counter is not cleared. Because the counter is not cleared, a later, unrelated excursion resumes from a partially advanced count and confirms a violation that no single excursion justifies. The trigger is a behavioural observation against a baselined design, not a supplier event and not a change in requirement.
